# workflow

A deterministic progression engine for step graphs. Go 1.27+.
Module: github.com/deepnoodle-ai/workflow. Root depends only on stdlib and
github.com/deepnoodle-ai/expr.

The engine is one pure function:

    func Apply(def *Definition, st *State, ev Event) (*State, []Command, error)

It does no I/O, starts no goroutines, reads no clock except ev.At, and never
modifies st. The run's clock is max(ev.At, st.UpdatedAt): an event stamped
earlier than the last one applied is applied at that time. Hosts persist
the returned State and Commands in one transaction and carry out the
commands after commit. Results come back as
events, at least once; duplicates are no-ops. The full host contract is
documentation/hosts.md; the "Host contract" section below says the same.
The API may change before v1.0 (0.x minor releases can break). The earlier
goroutine-based engine is github.com/deepnoodle-ai/workflow@v0.0.5.

## Packages

- workflow (root): Load, LoadMap, WithLimits, Apply, Abort, Outstanding,
  Resolve, State, Event, Command, StepID, StepError, StepErrorOf, RunError,
  Kinds, KindMap, KindSchemas, Limits; the handler contract both hosts call:
  Job{RunID string; Claims int; Command}, Handler func(ctx, Job) (any, error),
  ErrDeferred.
- local: Runner{Handlers map[string]workflow.Handler; Save func(ctx, runID,
  *State) error}. Start(ctx, runID, def, input) (*Run, error) (error =
  start rejected, e.g. ErrInvalidInput); Resume(ctx, runID, def, st) (*Run,
  error) re-dispatches in-flight work (deferred steps too) with Claims 2;
  Run(ctx, runID, def, input) (*State, error) = Start then Wait.
  *Run{ID}: Wait() (*State, error) (nil error once finished), Done() <-chan
  struct{}, Deliver(ev) error (ev.StepID may be a step name, resolved with
  Resolve; returns after Save of the new state, or Save's error; Resolve's
  or Apply's error, or ErrNotRunning after the run ends; zero At = now), Cancel(reason) error (= Deliver of EventCancel; finally
  steps run to the end; Force stops them; again = no-op), Pause(reason)
  error and Resume() error (hold the run: no handler is called for a new
  step or retry until Resume; a cancel ends the wait; Run.Resume releases a
  pause, Runner.Resume continues a saved run). ctx done = stop, not cancel:
  Wait returns the running state + ctx.Err(); Runner.Resume continues, and a
  paused run stays paused.
  Save is called with every changed state before its commands run.
- durable (root module; imports only the standard library and workflow):
  the types and errors every durable host backend shares. NewRun, Result
  (+ Jobs()), Run, StepRecord, StepStatus, Finished, SQLTx, JobRef,
  Execution, Observer, Settlement, Outcome, QueueStat, EventAborted,
  ErrorTypeDefinitionUnavailable, ErrRunNotFound, ErrRunExists,
  ErrUnstorable, ErrDefinitionUnavailable, ErrNotClaimable, ErrHardStop.
  Each backend declares them as aliases (postgres.Result =
  durable.Result), so errors.Is and type assertions work across backends;
  error messages start with "workflow:". Import it only for code that runs
  on any backend. The postgres module builds on internal packages of the
  root module: upgrade the root and postgres modules together, to the same
  release.
- postgres (separate module, pgx v5): Store (New(pool, kinds, opts...),
  Migrate, Start/StartTx, Deliver/DeliverTx, Cancel/CancelTx,
  Pause/PauseTx(ctx, runID, reason), Resume/ResumeTx(ctx, runID), GetRun,
  Steps, Events, QueueStats, ListRuns, DeleteEndedRuns, RunsChannel,
  NotifyChannel). StartSQLTx/DeliverSQLTx/CancelSQLTx/PauseSQLTx/ResumeSQLTx
  are the Tx forms for a database/sql transaction: they take SQLTx
  {ExecContext, QueryContext, Commit, Rollback}, which *sql.Tx and an Ent
  *Tx generated with sql/execquery satisfy (a *sql.DB does not compile);
  driver: pgx stdlib (stdlib.OpenDBFromPool(pool)). Options: WithSchema (default
  "workflow"), WithLimits (the only source of limits: the store loads every
  definition itself, from its document, with its kinds and limits),
  WithOnFinished(fn(ctx, tx, Finished) error) (runs in the finishing tx,
  after finally steps; Finished carries FinallyErrors),
  WithOnFinishedSQL(fn(ctx, tx SQLTx, Finished) error) (the one hook for
  code that also runs on sqlite: alone, the store opens its own
  transactions through database/sql on its pool, so fn runs on every path,
  with the caller's tx for the SQL forms and the store's *sql.Tx otherwise,
  and StartTx/DeliverTx/CancelTx are refused; with WithOnFinished too, a
  pgx.Tx calls WithOnFinished and a database/sql tx calls fn; a store with
  only WithOnFinished refuses the SQL forms), WithRunIDs(fn()
  string) (IDs for runs started without NewRun.ID; default UUIDv7). Start, Deliver and
  Cancel return *Result{RunID, State, Commands, Applied}: RunID is NewRun.ID
  or the generated one; Commands are already in the outbox (do not run them);
  Applied is false for a duplicate, late or finished-run event, a Start of
  an existing run, or a second cancel. Cancel is idempotent; Deliver an
  EventCancel with Force to stop finally steps. Worker{Store, Handlers
  map[string]workflow.Handler, ID, Concurrency, Lease, Poll, MaxClaims,
  Logger, ListenConfig, Observer, MayClaim}.Run(ctx). Handlers returning
  workflow.ErrDeferred finish the job; the step stays in flight until
  Store.Deliver. Cancelling Run's ctx is a hard stop (handlers cancelled;
  interrupted claims given back; a claim query in progress gets two more
  seconds, and its jobs are given back). Shutdown(ctx) error is the graceful
  stop: claim nothing more, let active jobs run until ctx is done, then
  cancel them and give their claims back (not counted toward MaxClaims);
  returns nil, or ctx's error if it cut jobs off, once every claim is
  settled or given back; Run then returns nil. Give Run its own context for
  that: if Run's ctx ends first, Run stops hard, and that Shutdown and every
  later one on the worker return ErrHardStop. A claim query hung past the
  deadline is cancelled 1 s later; if its claim had committed, its jobs are
  left to their lease and the claim counts toward MaxClaims.
  MayClaim func() bool, while false, claims nothing (timers included) and
  lets active jobs finish; reversible. Active() int counts active jobs
  (claimed, not yet settled or given back) plus claim queries in progress;
  with the gate closed, 0 means no claim is held.
  Observer{Claimed, Settled, Cancelled, LeaseLost, GivenBack, Abandoned
  func(job workflow.Job) (Settled also takes a Settlement{Outcome, Duration,
  Error *workflow.StepError}), ClaimError func(error)}: optional, called
  synchronously on worker goroutines, no metrics dependency. Each claim
  fires Claimed, then exactly one ending event, except a claim postponed for
  an unloadable definition. Outcome: OutcomeCompleted, OutcomeFailed,
  OutcomeDeferred, OutcomeFired. Duration is the handler's run time (zero
  for timers). Store.QueueStats(ctx) []QueueStat{Kind (CommandDispatchStep
  or CommandScheduleTimer), StepKind ("" for timers), Due, OldestDue}: per
  queue with any job, the claimable jobs and the oldest one's lag; poll from
  one process.
  For platforms that scale to zero: RunOnce(ctx) error runs the jobs due
  when it starts, timers included, plus the steps they dispatch with no
  delay (not timers that come due during the call, not outside work), up to
  Concurrency at once, then returns; a job error does not stop it; returns
  nil if Shutdown stopped it, else ctx's error, else the first claim or job
  error, else nil; no LISTEN. Execute(ctx, JobRef) (Execution{Settled bool,
  Jobs []JobRef}, error) runs one job for a task queue: nil error = done or
  nothing to do (2xx), any error = retry later (5xx); ErrNotClaimable when
  leased elsewhere, not due, no handler for the kind, or not claiming. If
  the ctx given to RunOnce or Execute ends, a handler that returns ctx's
  error or a retryable error has its claim given back, counted toward
  MaxClaims (only a Shutdown give-back is not counted). A handler that
  ignores ctx runs on; its heartbeat holds the lease until it returns or a
  Shutdown deadline passes, but only while the process gets CPU: where CPU
  is throttled after the request (Cloud Run request-based billing) the
  lease can run out and the step run twice (the fence drops the first
  result). Keep CPU allocated until the handler returns, or accept that.
  Both join Shutdown and Active.
  JobRef{RunID, StepID, Timer, StepKind, RunAt} (JSON); Result.Jobs()
  lists the jobs Start, Deliver and Cancel wrote; push them after commit.
  Resume's Result.Jobs() lists the timers it re-armed, then every running
  step of the run: held ones and ones a worker already runs (all queued
  already; push them again; a job pushed twice is claimed once, and a
  running one is found leased).
  RunsChannel() (<schema>_runs) is notified {"run_id","status"} on every
  status change; NotifyChannel() (<schema>_jobs) is notified with the run ID
  when jobs are written, and workers LISTEN on it. Run{ID, Workflow,
  DefinitionHash, Status, State, Metadata, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt,
  FinishedAt}. ListRuns(ctx, RunFilter{Status []RunStatus, Metadata
  map[string]any (top-level keys with equal string values; a non-string
  filter value is an error), CreatedAfter, CreatedBefore, UpdatedAfter
  (strict), Limit (0: 100, max 1000), Cursor}) (RunPage{Runs []RunSummary,
  Next}, error): newest created_at first, then ID; pass Next as Cursor until
  it is ""; no run repeats, and a run that matches the filter for the whole
  listing is not skipped (one that changes status while you page may be
  missed or appear on a later page); UpdatedAfter selects, it does not sort.
  RunSummary{ID, Workflow, DefinitionHash, Status, Metadata, Error
  (State.Error), CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, FinishedAt}: no state; use GetRun.
  DeleteEndedRuns(ctx, before) (int, error) deletes completed, failed and
  cancelled runs that ended before before, with their steps, events and
  jobs, 500 runs per transaction; never a run that has not ended; keeps
  definitions. No retention loop or option: call it from your own schedule.
  A deleted run's ID can start a new run. StepRecord{StepID, Step, StepKind,
  Index, Attempt, Status StepStatus (StepDispatched | StepCompleted |
  StepFailed | StepCancelled), Params, Item, Output, Error, NotBefore,
  DispatchedAt, SettledAt}. Errors:
  ErrRunNotFound, ErrRunExists, ErrUnstorable, ErrDefinitionUnavailable,
  ErrHardStop, ErrNotClaimable.
  Tables: definitions, runs, steps (kind = step kind), events, jobs (the
  outbox: one row per attempt or timer; jobs.kind is "step" or "timer",
  jobs.step_kind the step kind), schema_migrations. Jobs are fenced by a
  token that only grows. A step claimed MaxClaims times fails with type
  abandoned. A run whose definition no longer loads (ErrDefinitionUnavailable)
  is aborted with type definition_unavailable after MaxClaims, via Abort.
- sqlite (separate module; no driver import; tested with modernc.org/sqlite
  "sqlite" and mattn/go-sqlite3 "sqlite3"; SQLite 3.37+): the postgres host
  on SQLite, same API names and behaviour. New(db *sql.DB, kinds, opts...)
  with WithSchema (table prefix name_, default workflow_), WithLimits,
  WithRunIDs, WithOnFinishedSQL (runs on every path: the caller's tx for the
  SQL forms, the store's *sql.Tx otherwise). Store: Migrate, Start, Deliver,
  Cancel, Pause, Resume, StartSQLTx, DeliverSQLTx, CancelSQLTx, PauseSQLTx,
  ResumeSQLTx, GetRun, Steps, Events, QueueStats, ListRuns, DeleteEndedRuns
  (no pgx.Tx forms, RunsChannel, NotifyChannel). Worker: the postgres
  fields without ListenConfig; Run, Shutdown, Active, RunOnce, Execute.
  DSN: file:dev.db?_busy_timeout=5000&_journal_mode=WAL&_txlock=immediate
  (Migrate and Run refuse busy_timeout 0, and :memory: unless
  SetMaxOpenConns(1)). One writer for the whole database: a run lock blocks
  every write; keep a caller tx short. Wake-up: at once for jobs written
  through the same Store, else Poll. Clock: the process's. Under a lock held
  past a Shutdown deadline, a claim is left to its lease. mattn ignores ctx
  during a lock wait (each write waits up to busy_timeout; use 1000 ms).
  Processes on one host only; not on a network file system. Types and
  errors are durable's.
- decisions (separate module; github.com/deepnoodle-ai/workflow/decisions;
  depends on github.com/deepnoodle-ai/decide): Handler(client
  *decide.Client) Handler is the KindDecision handler:
  handlers[workflow.KindDecision] = decisions.Handler(client). One
  SystemOne request per distinct subject in the job (one when all share
  it), state = the subject text; decide -> Noul(question), answer its
  Noul; choose -> Choice(question, options...), answer its Choice.
  Returns {id: answer}; any error is decide's (the engine's 3 attempts
  retry it). Panics on a nil client. Guard(next Handler,
  GuardConfig) Handler asks a decision model about each job before next
  runs. GuardConfig{Client *decide.Client (required); Template
  *templates.Template (default templates.CommandRisk, which judges a shell
  command); Text func(Job) string (default: JSON of Config, Params, Item for
  an each step, "" when all are empty; "" blocks)}. Flagged: StepError
  guard_blocked, not retryable ("command-risk flagged destructive (yes
  97%), ..."), always; route with catch, e.g. to a step that asks a person.
  Guard has no hook to hold a flagged job; running it after approval is
  not supported (#98). The guard judges each job alone and does not limit
  a catch loop that retries a blocked step with new wordings; bound the
  loop with max_visits.
  No verdict (decide error, timeout, missing or invalid answer): next does
  not run; StepError guard_unavailable, retryable except for an
  *decide.APIError with a 4xx StatusCode other than 408 and 429, and
  decide's client-side ErrNoAPIKey and ErrInvalidRequest. Job text goes to
  the decide provider as request state only. Panics on nil next or Client,
  or a template that flags no question.

## Loading a definition

    def, err := workflow.Load(jsonBytes, workflow.KindMap{   // or workflow.LoadMap(yamlDecodedMap, kinds, opts...)
        "agent":  func(cfg map[string]any) error { ... },  // nil accepts anything
        "action": nil,
    }, workflow.WithLimits(workflow.Limits{MaxOutputBytes: 256 << 10, MaxStateBytes: 8 << 20})) // the defaults

Load returns *ValidationError{Problems []Problem{Step, Message}} with
every problem, and no definition. Apply returns ErrNotValidated for a
Definition not made by Load. A Definition is read-only once loaded; its
exported fields describe the document. def.Limits() returns the limits.
def.Hash() is a sha256 of the canonical document (LoadOptions and the
host's kinds are not part of it); State.DefinitionHash stores it.

workflow.RequireOutputs(schema) makes Load check the outputs against the
schema a caller needs, for a definition the host did not write, such as one
an agent generated for a step: LoadMap(doc, kinds,
workflow.RequireOutputs(job.OutputSchema)). A mismatch is a Problem marked
"(required by the caller)". A running run's graph never changes; generated
work runs as a child run (documentation/hosts.md, Generated workflows).

## Definition shape (JSON; YAML via LoadMap)

    {
      "name": "...", "description": "...",
      "input": <object schema | name>,      // the run's input, read as `input`; required and
                                           // property defaults validated/applied at Start
      "steps": [ <step>, ... ],            // first step is the start step
      "on_failure": [ <step>, ... ],       // run once, in order, when the run fails; `error` is bound
      "finally": [ <step>, ... ],          // run once, in order, after the outcome is decided; `run` is bound
      "outputs": {"k": "${{ expr }}",          // optional; default: latest value of each step a path ended at
                  "s": {"value": "${{ expr }}", "schema": <schema | name>, "description": "..."}},
      "schemas": {"name": <JSON schema>}   // named types
    }

Without "input", input is an untyped object. The engine has no notion of
what caused a run; a host that starts runs from events puts the event in
the input, e.g. {event: <provider payload>, meta: {type, source}}, read as
input.event.pull_request.number. A scheduled or manual run may pass none.

Step keys:
- name (identifier, unique across steps/on_failure/finally). Optional for
  on_failure and finally steps: they are named on_failure_1, finally_1, ...
  by position. Reserved names are rejected with a message saying why:
  globals and keywords (input, item, index, error, run, it, true, false,
  nil) and expression functions (len, split, filter, count, sort, map,
  any, all, find, try, if, coalesce, concat, ...).
- description: text for people; not passed in Command.Config
- exactly one kind key: a host kind ("agent": "reviewer", "action": "x") or
  "join": [names] | "set": value | "sleep": "1h" | "wait": true
- wait: true waits for a delivery: no handler; the delivered value is the
  step's value (typed and checked by output); timeout required (fails with
  type timeout); takes output, timeout, retry, catch, next, match,
  max_visits; no with/each; not in on_failure/finally; does not bound a
  cycle (a loop through a wait needs max_visits). Emits only its
  timeout ScheduleTimer (StepKind "wait"), no DispatchStep, so no step job.
  A retry waits again; a delivery during its backoff settles it.
- with: {..} templates, evaluated at dispatch (host kinds only)
- each: expr producing a list; concurrency: n; continue_on_error: bool
- output: <schema | basic type | schema name>  (host kinds, wait; validated on
  completion; sent as Command.OutputSchema)
- next: "name" | ["name", {"step": "name", "when": "bool expr"}]; match: "all" | "first"
  | {"switch": "expr", "cases": {"value": "step" | ["a","b"]}, "default": "step" | []}.
  when and switch may ask decisions (see Decisions below).
  Without match:, an edge with no when after a conditional edge is rejected
  (it reads as an else but is always followed): set match: first for
  if/else or match: all to follow both. Unconditional edges listed first are
  accepted.
- retry: {max_attempts, backoff: "1s", max_backoff: "5m", factor: 2, errors: [types]} | n
- catch: [{errors: [types], next: "name"}] | "name"
- timeout: "5m"; max_visits: n

Host-kind Config = the kind key plus every unreserved key (model,
instructions, ...), unevaluated. Reserved keys: name, description, output,
with, each, concurrency, continue_on_error, next, match, retry, catch,
timeout, max_visits, join, set, sleep, wait.

Types: Load type-checks every expression (expr's Program.Check) against
the input schema, step output schemas (or KindSchemas), inferred
set types, item/index, error. A step not settled on every path to the reader
is maybe-nil (the error says "may be nil here; use ?. or try(...)"): read
it with a?.f, try(a.f, fallback) (fallback when a.f fails to evaluate), or
coalesce(a, b) (non-nil when a and b are alternatives one of which must
have run). Expression language reference:
https://github.com/deepnoodle-ai/expr/blob/main/docs/reference/spec.md
outputs see a step as certain if no completing run can skip it. On paths only a catch leads to, the step's
value is {error: {type, message}}. when must be boolean; a switch must
cover its enum or have a default (number keys are JSON: "1000000"). with:
(absent = {}) is checked against the kind's params schema; unions must fit
in every variant. Optional KindSchemas interface on Kinds:
Schemas(kind, config) (params, output *Schema, error). ParseSchema(json).
Load copies host schemas before resolving refs; it never modifies them.
Schema problems in input: and outputs.<name>.schema name where they are;
defaults are checked everywhere, output schemas included.
Schema -> type: no type/enum ({} or true) = unchecked; false is rejected; type list = union of kinds
(null = nullable); enum = union of its values' kinds, filtered by type
(none left = nil); a value under an enum is kept as it is (no defaults);
{type: object} with no properties = open object (fields unchecked);
properties = closed object (undeclared keys pass validation and are
dropped where defaults apply), non-required without a default = maybe-nil,
with a default = never nil; default (checked against its schema at Load)
fills an absent or nil property of the input and of step outputs; $ref
takes only description and default beside it; additionalProperties
schema = open with that field type (read with ?.). Ref cycles (alias or
recursive) are rejected; inlined schemas are limited to 10000 nodes.
Outside the promise: untyped values (no schema, {}, input without an
input schema), list index out of range,
value errors (int("abc"), 1/0), number->integer and string->enum params
(checked at dispatch: invalid_params).
Runtime: input validated at Start (ErrInvalidInput), params at dispatch
(invalid_params), outputs at completion (invalid_output); absent declared
properties read as their default, else nil; every step name is in the env (nil until settled).
Outputs long form: an entry that is an object with a value or schema key
({value, schema, description}); the two forms mix. Load checks value's
type against schema like with: against params; at run completion each
value is validated: a mismatch fails the run (RunError type
invalid_output, no Step, on_failure runs). def.Outputs map[string]*Output
{Value any; Schema *Schema; Description string}; def.OutputSchema() *Schema
is the outputs as one JSON Schema object (all required, no others; nil
without outputs:), for exposing a workflow as a tool.

Expressions: each/when/switch are bare expr. with/set/outputs strings: no
${{ }} = literal; exactly one ${{ ... }} (no text or
spaces around it) = typed value; otherwise rendered text.
Only ${{ }} is a template: shell ${HOME} is text; $${{ writes a literal ${{.
Globals: input, steps by name, item/index in each with,
error in on_failure, run in finally: {status: "completed"|"failed"|"cancelled",
error: {step, step_id, type, message} or nil unless failed}. Extra functions: concat(lists...), coalesce(values...),
decide and choose (when/switch only, below);
expr's builtins include try(value, fallback).

Decisions: decide("question", subject) is the probability of yes (number
0..1, compare it: decide(...) > 0.8); choose("question", subject, ["a",
"b"]) is one option, typed as their enum (a switch must cover it). Only in
next when/switch, not in list-function bodies or a subject. Question and
options are literals (at least two options, distinct and non-empty). Load
types each subject alone and rejects a read of a possibly-nil value: every
decision is asked before routing, so a guard in the condition does not
protect it (write x?.body, or pass x). Other run-time failures (x[0] on
an empty x) fail the run. Load needs the host's Kinds to know KindDecision
("decision"); no step may have that kind. When the step settles, Apply
evaluates every call's subject (no short-circuit: match first, &&, ||, if,
try skip none), dedupes on (function, question, subject text, options),
and emits one DispatchStep: StepID "<node>.next#N" (Unit "<node>.next",
Step the step), StepKind "decision", Index -1, Params {"questions": [{id,
type: "decide"|"choose", question, subject, options?}]}, OutputSchema; a
ScheduleTimer bounds it. subject is text: a string as is, else JSON with
sorted keys. The handler returns {id: answer}; decisions.Handler(client) is
one built on decide. Wrong, missing or extra
answers: invalid_output. A decision gets 3 attempts; any failure uses
one; after the third, the step fails. The path waits at the step (joins
wait for it); the answers are saved in state (keyed by ID, with the
question; no subject copy) and routing reads them, so a replay never asks
again. Retry/timeout: always 3 attempts of 1m, never the step's. A failed
decision fails the step (value {error: ...}; catch applies; on a control
step the run fails). Do not wrap the decision handler in a guard. Not a visit; answers are not readable by later steps.
Keyword field names work: error.type.

Semantics:
- Multiple matching edges fork the path: it goes on to one target (the one
  it left the fork along last time, if the path is back and that target
  matched; else the first whose branch a join on the way back names, else
  the first that can reach the fork again, else the first) and each other
  target starts a child named "<path>.<target>", "~N" from the second time.
  No match ends the path. Run completes when all paths end. Ended paths
  nothing can read are dropped, so a loop that forks keeps bounded state.
- join is synchronization plus an assertion. It waits until no live path
  can still reach it (in the current pass of the loops it is in), then
  merges arrivals onto the arrival the others forked from, or onto the
  arrival with the lowest ID if none did. The names are not what it waits
  for: they are steps that must have settled on some arriving
  path, which also makes them safe to read downstream. join: [] names
  nothing. Load rejects a name a path can skip (on a when branch, past a
  branch whose conditional edges may all fail, on one switch case, or one a
  catch route bypasses): "join: X may not have settled when the join fires
  ...". Each condition counts as possibly true or false on its own. Loop
  back edges are not followed, so the run-time failure (type "join")
  remains as a backstop for joins in loops.
- loops: a join fires once per pass of the loops it is in (a pass starts
  when a path enters the loop's head). It waits for paths that can still
  arrive in that pass, including paths going around loops it is not in.
  Named steps must have settled in the current pass of the loops they share
  with the join. Load rejects a join in a loop with several entry steps.
- each: one DispatchStep per item, parallel up to concurrency; output is the
  list of item outputs in order. An item failure (after retries) fails the step
  at once: items in flight get CancelStep, pending items are skipped, and
  late results for them are ignored. With continue_on_error, failed items
  become {error: {type, message}} instead.
- Retry only when declared AND StepError.Retryable AND type matches. New
  DispatchStep with Attempt+1 and NotBefore = At + backoff. Apply is exact;
  the durable hosts add up to 20% jitter to retry backoff (at most 1m), on
  top of max_backoff, and move the retry's timeout timer with it. Later is
  safe, never earlier. State keeps the exact time, so Outstanding ignores
  host jitter; a host that re-drives work takes due times from its jobs.
- timeout: ScheduleTimer with the attempt's StepID; on TimerFired the attempt
  gets CancelStep and fails with type "timeout" (retryable). Once the attempt
  settles the timer is obsolete; hosts may drop it, and a late TimerFired is
  a no-op.
- catch routes a terminal failure; the step's value becomes {error: {...}}.
- Run failure cancels everything in flight, then runs on_failure. An
  on_failure failure sets RunError.OnFailure and stops on_failure.
- Cancel: CancelStep for all in flight, no on_failure (a cancel during
  on_failure cancels it and the run is cancelled); then finally. A cancel
  decides the outcome once: a second cancel (a redelivery) changes nothing
  and the finally steps run to the end. Force: true also skips the finally
  steps (each in FinallyErrors, type "cancelled").
- Pause (EventPause, Reason): running -> paused, State.Reason = reason.
  Resume (EventResume): paused -> running, Reason cleared. Each is a no-op
  for any other status. Apply advances a paused run as a running one
  (results, sleeps, joins, dispatches); the host must not start a
  dispatched step of a paused run (durable claims skip its step jobs;
  timers are still claimed). A step timeout that fires while paused does
  not fail the attempt; Resume re-arms it with a ScheduleTimer at Resume
  time + timeout. A timer that has not fired keeps its deadline. Cancel works on a
  paused run. A decided outcome (last path ends, or a failure for good)
  ends the pause: on_failure and finally start with no Resume. Paused is
  not Terminal(); its Outcome() is "".
- finally: steps run in order once the outcome is decided (completed after
  outputs are evaluated; failed after on_failure; cancelled after in-flight
  work is cancelled). Same shapes as on_failure (host kinds and set; with,
  output, retry, timeout; no next/catch/each/join/sleep/wait). They read run,
  every step/on_failure step as maybe-nil, and earlier finally steps (a
  failed one reads as {error: {type, message}}); not error, outputs or
  later finally steps. Each runs even if an earlier one failed. A failure
  never changes the outcome: it is appended to State.FinallyErrors and
  Command.FinallyErrors ([]*RunError) on the terminal command. Status while
  they run: completing | failing | cancelling; the terminal command comes
  after the last one. A plain cancel during finally is a no-op. A cancel
  with Force during finally cancels the step in flight, skips the rest
  (each reported, type "cancelled") and finishes with the
  outcome already decided (completed stays completed, with outputs).
  A host that ends a run with Abort skips them: the postgres host's aborts
  (definition_unavailable, abandoned timers and unfailable steps).

## Events and commands

    type Event struct {
        At time.Time; Kind EventKind  // start | step_completed | step_failed | timer_fired | cancel | pause | resume
        Input map[string]any           // start; read as `input`
        StepID StepID; Output any; Error *StepError  // step events
        Reason string; Force bool      // cancel, pause; Force stops or skips finally steps
    }
    type StepError struct { Type, Message string; Retryable bool }
    type Command struct {
        Kind CommandKind  // dispatch_step | cancel_step | schedule_timer | run_completed | run_failed | run_cancelled
        StepID StepID; Step, StepKind string
        Params, Config map[string]any; Item any; Index int (-1 without each); Attempt int
        NotBefore time.Time            // dispatch: retry backoff; timer: fire time
        Outputs map[string]any; Error *RunError; Reason string
        FinallyErrors []*RunError      // any terminal command
    }
    type RunError struct { Step string; StepID StepID; Type, Message string; OnFailure *RunError; At time.Time }

StepID names one attempt: <path>/<step>[@<visit>][[<index>]]#<attempt>,
e.g. main/verify[3]#1, main.tests/lint@2#1. on_failure steps run on path
failure (failure/page#1), finally steps on path finally
(finally/release#1). Unique within its run only. id.Unit() is the StepID
without #attempt (main/verify[3]; the same for every attempt, a retry keeps
it), id.Step() the step name, id.Attempt() the number. Two host keys:
attempt key = run ID + StepID (jobs, step records, deduplicating results);
unit key = run ID + StepID.Unit() (idempotency keys for side effects outside
the host, e.g. a payment provider's). Do not key side effects on the StepID:
a retry has a new one.

Abort(st, err *RunError, at) (*State, []Command): fails a run a host cannot
advance with Apply, without the definition, so neither on_failure nor
finally runs. Commands: CancelStep per attempt in flight (no StepKind), then
RunFailed. Outputs and Reason are cleared. A run not started or finished
is returned unchanged.

Apply errors (host mistakes, state unchanged): ErrNotValidated,
ErrDefinitionMismatch, ErrNotStarted, ErrUnknownStep, ErrInvalidEvent,
ErrInvalidInput. A duplicate or late event returns (st, nil, nil) with the
same pointer. Apply takes only a StepID.

Resolve(def, st, id StepID) (StepID, error): Event.StepID is a StepID or a
step name ("approve"). A StepID passes through; a name resolves to the step's
one running attempt; with none running and the latest visit completed, to that
attempt (Apply then ignores the event as a duplicate), except for a step in a
loop, which gets ErrNotWaiting (between visits a repeat and an early answer
look the same; deliver the full StepID to repeat); ErrNotWaiting when the run
has not reached the step, or its latest visit failed, timed out or was
cancelled ("no longer waiting"); ErrInvalidEvent when more than one attempt
runs (message lists them); ErrUnknownStep for a name that is not a step. Hosts
call it before Apply on the locked state and store the resolved StepID; local
Run.Deliver and every durable Deliver form do.

Determinism: the same ordered event stream gives the same states and
commands. Successful completions of steps in flight together may arrive in
any order and reach the same final state and dispatches (property tests).
Not for failures and timeouts: a failure that arrives before a sibling's
success fails the run before that success dispatches anything after it, and
a timeout races its step's result.

Limits: MaxOutputBytes caps one step output or set value; MaxStateBytes caps
State.Bytes, the outputs, set values and each items the state holds now. A
step visit a newer visit of the same step superseded (a loop pass) is dropped
from the state with its bytes, so a poll/sleep loop runs indefinitely;
results for a dropped visit are ignored as late. State is not a history.

Library error types: timeout, expression, output_too_large,
state_too_large, join, max_visits, switch, invalid_output, invalid_params,
cancelled (finally steps a cancel stopped, in FinallyErrors).

## State

JSON-serializable. The supported read view: DefinitionHash (JSON key
"definition"), Status (running | paused | completing | failing | cancelling |
completed | failed | cancelled), Input, StartedAt, FinishedAt, UpdatedAt,
Outputs, Error, Reason (pause or cancel reason), FinallyErrors, Bytes. Paths, visits
and joins are unexported bookkeeping, serialized but not API. Before v1.0 a
minor release may change the stored format (release notes say so).
Helpers: st.InFlight() []StepID, st.Unit(id) *Unit (nil if unknown,
replaced by a retry, or dropped by a loop), RunStatus.Terminal()
(completed/failed/cancelled only), RunStatus.Outcome() (completing ->
completed, failing -> failed, cancelling -> cancelled).
Outstanding(def, st) rebuilds DispatchStep/ScheduleTimer commands for
in-flight work; none for a run not started or finished (a finished run's
definition hash is still checked).

## Host contract (same as documentation/hosts.md)

1. Persist state, step records and commands (outbox) in the event's
   transaction; lock the run row. Skip the write when Apply returns the
   same state pointer.
2. Carry out commands only after commit.
3. Deliver results at least once.
4. An attempt may be dispatched again: key side effects outside the host
   on run ID + StepID.Unit(), records and jobs on run ID + StepID.
5. Store definitions by hash; a run keeps its version.
6. Resolve a step name with Resolve before Apply, in the same transaction;
   store the event with the resolved StepID.

Commands: DispatchStep = run the attempt not before NotBefore, report
StepCompleted/StepFailed. ScheduleTimer = deliver TimerFired for StepID at
NotBefore (sleep, timeout; a wait emits only its timeout timer). CancelStep =
stop the attempt if possible, drop its timer; a late result is ignored.
RunCompleted/RunFailed/RunCancelled = the run is over (on_failure and finally
done); alert on FinallyErrors. Keep carrying out commands until Status is
terminal.

Handlers (both hosts): Handler func(ctx, Job) (any, error). Job{RunID, Claims,
Command}: Claims > 1 means an earlier call may have done part of the work
(postgres reclaimed a lost lease; local resumed). Return the output; a
*StepError sets type and retryable; any other error is retryable type "error"
(StepErrorOf); no handler = unknown_kind, panic = panic (not retryable).
Return ErrDeferred to hand off: the step stays in flight until its result is
delivered (local: Run.Deliver; postgres: Store.Deliver; by StepID or step
name) or its timeout fires. A handler that would only return ErrDeferred is
better a wait step. ctx is cancelled when the attempt is no longer wanted.

Deploys and versioning: the hash covers the authored document only. Kind
schemas (KindSchemas) are not pinned: every load, including a postgres
reload after a deploy, uses the host's current kinds. A kind's params and
output schema is the host's contract: change it compatibly (add optional
fields) or ship a new kind name (payments.charge.v2) and keep the old one
until its runs finish. A definition that no longer loads makes its runs
unavailable (postgres: ErrDefinitionUnavailable, then an abort after
MaxClaims). Handlers must tolerate an attempt being dispatched again.
